title: Modern Walnut Kitchen
shortDescription: Floor-to-ceiling walnut cabinetry with integrated appliances and a waterfall island.
description: This Portland kitchen was a complete gut-renovation. The brief was to create a seamless, furniture-grade kitchen where every appliance disappears behind custom cabinetry. We milled the walnut doors in-house from Oregon-grown black walnut, carefully bookmatching the grain across the island panels for a continuous flow of figure.
challenge: The ceiling height varied by nearly 3 inches across the room, and the exterior wall had a non-standard bow. Every upper cabinet run required individual scribing to maintain level sight lines.
solution: We pre-scribed each upper cabinet run in the shop using a full-scale site template, then made final adjustments on-site. The waterfall island edge is formed from a single slab to eliminate visible seams.

title: Master Bedroom Suite
shortDescription: Custom oak wardrobes, bedside tables, and a matching vanity unit for a heritage home.
description: A complete bedroom furniture suite for a 1920s heritage home in Seattle. The brief called for furniture that felt as though it had always belonged in the house — not an afterthought, but a natural continuation of the home's original character. We used straight-grained white oak throughout and matched the profile of the existing door casings.
challenge: The existing walls were not plumb or square, and the alcoves designated for the wardrobes varied by up to half an inch over their full height.
solution: Each wardrobe unit was built as a freestanding carcase with a scribing panel that could be trimmed to the wall. This allowed perfect installation without altering the original plasterwork.

title: Upscale Restaurant Bar
shortDescription: 90-foot mahogany bar counter with carved apron detail and backlit display shelving.
description: A landmark hospitality project in San Francisco's Financial District. The bar counter runs 90 feet around a central service well and serves as the visual anchor of the entire 200-seat restaurant. The mahogany was selected for its deep reddish-brown tone and its ability to accept the client's custom stain formula, which ties the bar to the dining room's colour palette.
challenge: The curved section of the bar — a 20-foot radius sweep — required building a custom radius jig and steam-bending the apron rails in-shop. No straight lumber was used in the curved section.
solution: We built a full-scale radius template on-site first, then returned to the shop to steam-bend all rails and face frames to exact spec. Final fit was within a millimetre throughout.

title: Home Library Built-ins
shortDescription: Walnut library wall with rolling ladder, integrated reading nook, and coffered ceiling detail.
description: A private home library for an academic client in Portland. The brief was unambiguous: make it feel like a room from a Victorian gentlemen's club, but scaled for a 14-foot residential ceiling. We used American black walnut throughout, with hand-carved acanthus corbels at each pilaster and a fully functional rolling brass ladder that travels on a recessed ceiling track.
challenge: The 14-foot ceiling height required scaffolding for the full installation, and the structural header above the original doorway had to be boxed out before we could continue the shelving run across it.
solution: We engineered the upper shelf runs on a concealed steel framework anchored at the floor and ceiling, allowing the full walnut face to be load-bearing in appearance only. This eliminated the need for wall fasteners that would have compromised the original plaster.

title: Cedar Deck & Pergola
shortDescription: Multi-level Western red cedar deck with a freestanding pergola and built-in bench seating.
description: A multi-level outdoor living space for a lakeside residence in Lake Oswego. The upper level connects directly to the kitchen through wide French doors; the lower level steps down to a fire-pit seating area. The freestanding pergola was engineered to carry a retractable canvas awning system and is anchored with concealed steel post bases that keep the footings invisible from any viewing angle.
challenge: The steep slope of the lot required a 7-foot drop from the upper deck to the lower level, creating a structural engineering challenge and a visual massing problem — the lower deck risked looking like a platform floating in mid-air.
solution: We used heavy timber framing with 6×6 posts and exposed beam connections to give the lower structure visual weight. Planted built-in bench seating along the perimeter creates a natural enclosure while hiding the structural footings from view at ground level.

title: Farmhouse Dining Table
shortDescription: 12-seat live-edge black walnut dining table with hand-forged steel base for a farmhouse estate.
description: A statement dining table commissioned for a farmhouse estate in the Willamette Valley. The slab came from a single black walnut tree felled on the property, milled on-site and air-dried for 14 months before we began work. The live edge was preserved exactly as it came from the tree; we only stabilised two small voids with black-tinted epoxy to maintain structural integrity without altering the silhouette.
challenge: At 14 feet long and 48 inches wide, the slab's natural moisture variation created a 3/8-inch cup across the width after final drying. Standard flattening would have removed too much material.
solution: We flattened the slab using a combination of a wide-bed CNC router and hand planing, removing the cup without reducing the slab below its target thickness. The steel base legs were built with a slight inward lean to allow the slab's slight seasonal movement without stressing the joints.

title: Executive Office Suite
shortDescription: Cherry wood partner desk, credenza, and floor-to-ceiling bookcase for a law firm's managing partner.
description: A full office suite for a managing partner at a Portland law firm. The client specified American cherry for its warmth and its ability to develop a rich patina over decades of use. The partner desk is built as a traditional kneehole design with dovetail-joined drawers and a leather-inlaid top. The credenza behind continues the cherry, with tambour doors that roll into the cabinet body and disappear entirely.
challenge: The office has floor-to-ceiling glazing on two sides, which created a thermal environment where temperature fluctuates significantly — a serious risk for solid wood case goods that would warp or crack in less stable conditions.
solution: We engineered all panel components with a plywood core and solid cherry face veneer, then used a floating-panel construction method that allows the cherry faces to expand and contract without stressing the carcases.

title: Custom Entertainment Center
shortDescription: Built-in media wall in white oak with integrated TV frame, speaker grilles, and concealed storage.
description: A media wall that doubles as a room divider between the open-plan living and dining areas of a Beaverton new-build. The brief was for the television to be framed, not simply mounted — to give it the appearance of a piece of art rather than an appliance. Flanking the TV, full-height white oak panels conceal a 7.1 surround sound speaker system behind acoustically transparent grille cloth backed with oak veneer.
challenge: Routing all speaker cables, HDMI runs, and power through the wall without visible conduits required coordination with the electricians before the drywall was closed.
solution: We provided full millwork drawings to the electrical sub ahead of rough-in, specifying exact conduit locations and pull-box positions so every wire emerged exactly where needed when the casework was installed.

title: Shaker Kitchen Remodel
shortDescription: Classic shaker-style cabinetry in painted maple with a quartzite island and integrated wine storage.
description: A full kitchen remodel for a couple who had lived with a dated 1990s kitchen for 12 years before deciding to invest in something permanent. The brief was classic but not old-fashioned: five-piece shaker doors in hand-painted eggshell on maple, a waterfall quartzite island, and a wine storage column integrated into the pantry wall.
challenge: The existing soffits were structural and could not be removed, limiting the upper cabinet height. The clients wanted tall uppers but the soffits were in the way.
solution: We designed the upper cabinets to incorporate the soffit cleanly — rather than hiding it, we framed it with moulding to make it look like an intentional architectural feature, and used that same moulding as a cornice detail across all the upper runs.

title: Boutique Hotel Lobby
shortDescription: Feature reception desk and wall panelling in smoked oak for a 40-room boutique hotel in Seattle.
description: The lobby of a newly opened boutique hotel in Seattle's Capitol Hill neighbourhood. The design brief called for a material palette of smoked oak, blackened steel, and honed marble — materials associated with high craft but without the formality of traditional luxury hotels. The reception desk is the centrepiece: a curved form 14 feet wide with a smoked oak face and a marble counter surface with integrated LED lighting below the counter lip.
challenge: The curved reception desk required continuous smoked oak veneer panels around a compound curve. Standard veneer would not bend to the required radius without cracking, particularly at the 6-inch reveal at the top of the desk face.
solution: We used flexible backed veneer on the curved panels and developed a two-part substrate — an MDF primary former covered with a secondary kerf-cut MDF skin that allowed the necessary flex. All panel seams were aligned with the desk's design joints so they disappeared entirely in the finished piece.

title: Coastal Beach House Kitchen
shortDescription: Open-plan kitchen in cerused white oak with integrated dining and a 16-foot pantry wall.
description: A complete kitchen and dining integration for a beach house on the Oregon coast. The owners wanted the kitchen, island, and dining area to feel like one continuous space rather than three separate zones. We achieved this by running the same cerused white oak cabinetry and dining banquette as a single uninterrupted millwork element around three walls of the space.
challenge: The coastal environment brings extreme humidity variation — from saturated ocean air in winter to very dry summer conditions — which creates significant dimensional movement in solid wood. All joinery had to accommodate movement without restricting it.
solution: We used rift-sawn white oak throughout for its dimensional stability, and all panel-to-frame connections were designed with floating tenons and expanded mortises. The ceruse finish also acts as a stabilising layer on the surface.

title: Wine Cellar & Tasting Room
shortDescription: Climate-controlled wine cellar with 800-bottle racking system and an adjoining tasting room in Douglas fir.
description: A custom wine cellar and tasting room built into an existing basement for a wine collector and restaurateur in Portland. The racking system holds 800 bottles across a combination of individual diamond bins, case storage, and display rows with label-forward display for 48 showcase bottles. The adjoining tasting room is finished in reclaimed Douglas fir salvaged from a demolished warehouse in Northwest Portland.
challenge: The basement had an existing concrete floor with a drain in a non-optimal location, and the HVAC penetrations for the wine cellar cooling unit could not be relocated. Both had to be integrated invisibly into the finished design.
solution: We designed the racking layout to incorporate the drain within a central service corridor that is concealed behind a full-width storage cabinet. The HVAC penetrations were boxed in Douglas fir and given the same profile as the overhead beam boxings, so they read as architectural features.
